posts.author: Thecomical
posts.body: Hello! Umm… I’m new here, and I have a game story idea in mind, but I have no idea how to start or what to do first. Could you give some advice to a beginner like me? And also, for things like characters—do I need to hire an artist, or how does that work?" Thank you

posts.author: SirLobo
posts.body:
First, welcome to the community!
Well, this question can be quite ambiguous. Each dev has their own perspective, and each perspective is not necessarily a rule (except for some obvious things that are really important, like genuinely wanting to learn and being able to listen, absorb opposing opinions),
BUT... here's my 2 cents for you:
First of all:
create the concept idea. Ideally, RPG Maker can be used to make a lot of kinds of game genres, but for your first project, I recommend using RPG Maker to make an... RPG (or something similar). It doesn’t need to be anything grand or epic, it just needs to be well written and developed. Players should be able to empathize even with the villains — every character should be unique in the way they act, speak, and express themselves. You don’t need dozens of characters and villains either; develop half a dozen and you’ll be fine! I recommend getting a book on storytelling (or just studying online and on YouTube).
Don't worry about artists right now, you can use the default assets from the RTP and tools. VX Ace has a built-in character generator. Alternatively, the internet also offers many free resources that you can use, just google it!
Avoid using plugins that use complex systems like real-time battles or something similar. Try to primarily focus on the STORY. So, plugins are cool and can seem like a good solution for new ideas, but maintaining them, but combined with a lack of skill in basic aspects this can frustrate you and even push you away from game development. Be very careful: separate what is a viable idea from what is an unviable one
Make a short‑scope project. Of course, set goals, but don’t pressure yourself; everything takes time. The important thing is to complete the project, whether it takes one week or six months. What matters is reaching the conclusion, whether it’s simple or not. And of course, later on, share it with the community to get positive feedback!
Have fun during the process — the important thing is to finish the project without psychological pressure.
Best regards!

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum! You already got some good advice.
I will just say from my own experience that taking the time to really learn the tool and what it can do is very important. Recreate tutorials, thoroughly explore the default Event Commands options (what they do and how they work), experiment and try things out, and ask questions when needed.
Once you have taken the time to learn the tool with an experiments project, you can really make some good headway on a very small game to get end to end experience.
Anyway, just my additional 2 pennies.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!
